proof: `BOARD OF ASSESSORS`, PDF page 12 of the FY2011 annual town report (printed page 9). TABLE 1 of five, headed `Fiscal 2011 Assessments and Revenues by Major Property Class`. The printed column header, verbatim and in order: `Property Class` | `Levy Percent` | `Valuation by Class` | `Tax Rate` | `Tax Levy`. Open Space prints `-0-` in both money columns -- an explicit zero, recorded as 0. THREE identities close on this page and they are independent of one another: (a) the five levy percentages sum to the printed `100.0000`; (b) the five tax levies sum to the printed `18,006,811.48` to the cent; (c) each class's valuation at the printed rate of 16.16 per thousand reproduces that class's printed tax levy to the cent -- 1,000,004,500 x 16.16/1000 = 16,160,072.72, 64,514,700 -> 1,042,557.55, 21,614,900 -> 349,296.78, 28,148,789 -> 454,884.43. THE PAGE'S OWN TOTALS CELL FOR VALUATION IS MISPRINTED. It reads `1,114,2828,889` -- ten digits, which no reading of the five components produces and which is not a number the town uses anywhere else. Verified by re-reading the cell at 6x: the characters are `1,114,2828,889`. The total used here, 1,114,282,889, is the figure the SAME PAGE prints twice more: the `Valuation and Tax History` row for 2011 (`Total Valuation 1,114,282,889`) and the `Fiscal Year 2011 Abstract of Assessments` TOTALS row. The five components sum to it exactly. So the total is read off the document, not inferred, and the garbled cell is recorded as a defect in the published report rather than corrected into the figures.
